minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  January 20, 2014

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Kelley at 5:04 p.m., on January 20, 2014, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on January 17, 2014, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:10 p.m.)
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel: Anticipated Litigation Initiation of Litigation
  Pursuant to Subdivision (c) of Section 54956.9: One Potential Case.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.
City Council Minutes  1  January 20, 2014
 PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

INVOCATION: Mayor Kelley

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council received an update and gave instructions to
staff. His office will follow up and report back to the Council once the research is done. Mr.
Curley noted that the Council may take further action at a later date.

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Business of the Month - Albertsons Stores

  Mayor Kelley presented proclamations to Albertsons store Managers Robin Begley-Leon
  and Todd Broom.

P2. Presentation by Allison Tran on Mission Viejo’s Teen Voice Blog

  Teen Services Librarian, Allison Tran presented on overview of the Teen Voice
  Blog. Students Danielle Kelly and Danielle Leard discussed their experience writing for
  the blog.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Dave Sanford, American Heart Association Passion Committee Volunteer, M.V.: announced that
February is Heart Awareness month and he encouraged local shop owners to display the red
dress logo and distribute informational fliers to help create awareness of heart disease which is
the number one killer for women. He asked the Council to consider lighting city hall in red for
the month of February and to host a reception in the patio garden or main lobby of City Hall at
6:00 p.m. on February 1 so the Council can flip the switch to kick off the red lighting. Lastly,
Mr. Sanford asked the City to provide the Saddleback Room for two CPR training sessions and
to issue a proclamation declaring February 7, 2014, as “Wear Red for Women Day.”

Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: announced an upcoming golf tournament, Tradition Never Graduates,
which will benefit the present and future football players of Mission Viejo High School. The
tournament will be held on February 24, 2014, at the Mission Viejo Country Club. Mrs.
Bucknum invited residents to golf and local businesses to sponsor the event and she noted that
further information is available at www.missionfootball.com.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: asked the City Council to reconsider their vote to approve the JPA
amendment to the OCFA contract for equitable adjustment. He stated that new information has
come out since the Council voted and he recommended that Mission Viejo conduct its own
actual cost study.

City Council Minutes  2  January 20, 2014
 CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3, 4, 6, and 10 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of January 6, 2014, as
  presented.

5.  Check Register Dated January 3, 2014 in the Amount of $1,836,583.79

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

7.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for November 2013

  Received and filed.

8.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for November 2013

  Received and filed.

9.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for
  November 2013

  Received and filed.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

City Council Minutes  3  January 20, 2014
 OLD BUSINESS

11. Award a contract for construction of the Mission Viejo Cattery Building Expansion
  (CIP 318)

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Karen Frazier, animal shelter volunteer, M.V.: expressed support for the cattery expansion
  project.

  Council Member Schlicht requested that this decision be postponed to the next Council
  Meeting. She stated that she doesn't feel that taxpayer dollars should be going to other
  cities and Mission Viejo should not subsidize Laguna Niguel to the tune of $200,000.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, (1) to
  award a contract to IBN Construction and issue a purchase order to IBN Construction in an
  amount not to exceed $360,500; and (2) approve the First Amendment to the Operating
  Agreement with the City of Aliso Viejo and authorize the Mayor to execute the contracts
  subject to any minor revisions.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, seconded by Council Member Ury, to move the
  previous question.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

  On roll call, said MAIN motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

  Council Member Schlicht announced that she voted no because Mission Viejo is giving
  monies away to credit Laguna Niguel and sometime in the future the City’s General Funds
  are going to have to backfill that gift.

12. Independent Accountant’s Report on Applying Cal Card Agreed-Upon Procedures

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report and answered
  the City Council Member's questions.

City Council Minutes  4  January 20, 2014
   Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to receive
  and file the report.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

13. Pension and Retiree Insurance Program Valuations and Discussion of Unfunded
  Liabilities

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report and answered
  questions of the City Council.

  Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Council Member Schlicht, to
  receive the report and approve staff's recommendation to reduce the amortization period of
  the Retiree Health Benefit Plan from eleven years to seven years.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

RECESS

At the hour of 8:06 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:17
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

3.  Check Register Dated December 13, 2013 in the Amount of $2,027,364.71

4.  Check Register Dated December 20, 2013 in the Amount of $2,097,774.02

  Council Member Schlicht announced that she will be voting no on agenda items 3 and 4 in
  protest to the ITF Wheelchair Masters expenditures. She noted that she would still like to
  see a balance sheet for the event.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to ratify the
  accompanying check registers (items 3 and 4.)

City Council Minutes  5  January 20, 2014
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

6.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for November 2013

  Council Member Schlicht asked if the payroll disbursement of $1.18 million was the entire
  payroll for the month of November.

  Director Dyas responded that that figure represents the entire payroll for all pay periods in
  the month.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to receive
  and file the report.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

10. Revisions to the City of Mission Viejo Personnel Policies

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht expressed concern with paragraph D on page 4 of attachment
  A. She asked if we are 100% sure that all personnel who deal with children have had a
  background check.

  Mrs. Dyas confirmed that that is the policy and staff also requires that anyone working in
  the library, including volunteers, have a background check as well.

  Council Member Schlicht referred to page 5, paragraph 3 and asked if "may be terminated"
  should be changed to "shall be terminated."

  Director Dyas noted that it depends on the circumstances and that there may be a valid
  explanation in some cases. By consensus the Council agreed to continue with the use of the
  word may.

City Council Minutes  6  January 20, 2014
   Council Member Schlicht asked that the City Attorney be included in paragraph VI A2 on
  page 8 (Record Storage,) paragraph 3 on page 8 (Record Dissemination) and paragraph VII
  B1 (Confidentiality - Record Storage.)

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to adopt
  Resolution 14-06, as amended, Providing for the Revisions to Personnel Policies.

  Amendments: Exhibit A, Criminal Background Checks/Criminal History Policy, add "City
  Attorney" to paragraph VI A2 on page 8 (Record Storage,) paragraph 3 on page 8 (Record
  Dissemination) and paragraph VII B1 on page 9 (Confidentiality - Record Storage.)

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

 14. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: complimented the Council on reducing the City's pension
  liability and stated that it pales in comparison to the OCFA pension liability which is $655
  million. Mr. Wontrobski asked what Mission Viejo's share of that liability is. He also
  discussed fire maps and announced that he was recently assessed a homeowners association
  increase due to conformance with the fire maps. Lastly, Mr. Wontrobski noted that the City
  of Irvine rejected the phase in program for OCFA's equitable adjustment, then OCFA said
  there was enough money so they didn't have to phase in.

  Mayor Kelley presented the OCFA report.

15. Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Reardon presented the report.

16. San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Reardon presented the report.

17. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

City Council Minutes  7  January 20, 2014
 18. Orange County Vector Control District

  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness presented the report.

19. CUSD Ad Hoc Committee - CFD 87-1 Mello-Roos Tax Update

  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness and Mayor Kelley presented an update on the efforts to end CFD
  87-1 Mello-Roos taxes for Mission Viejo and Aliso Viejo residents.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

20. Status Update on Medix Ambulance Service, Inc.

  City Manager Wilberg presented the report.

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that the City Manager can help everyone by attaching
  information from the OCFA Technical Advisory Committee to his City Manager's reports.
  In doing so, the City Manager could warn the City Council and the public of potential
  problems.

  Michael Dimas, Medix Ambulance Service, Inc., M.V.: answered the City Council
  Members questions regarding his plans to sell Medix Ambulance Service.

  There was no action taken on this matter.

21. Business Change: City Attorney Support Firm

  City Manager Wilberg and City Attorney Curley presented the staff report.

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that the time is right to conduct an RFP process for City
  Attorney services. He noted that the market for legal services is very competitive and that
  law firms are actively looking for new clients.

  Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Council Member Ury, to (1)
  terminate the present representation agreement with Richards, Watson & Gershon
  (Richards, Watson & Gershon respects the decision to broaden the services that the City
  Attorney can offer to the City and has no objection to the termination and release of the
  contract,) and (2) authorize the execution of exactly the same business engagement contract
  (other than necessary updates, changing of names, dates and grammar necessitated
  changes); engaging Bill Curley and Lozano Smith to represent the City.

City Council Minutes  8  January 20, 2014
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

City Attorney’s Report

City Attorney Bill Curley provided an update on the County's ordinance to prevent sex offenders
from entering public parks. He noted that the County's ordinance has recently been challenged in
Superior Court and in the Court of Appeal and that the District Attorney is going to appeal that
decision to the Supreme Court. Mr. Curley recommended that the City maintain the status quo
with its own "sex offenders in public parks" ordinance and wait to see what the State Supreme
Court does with the County's ordinance. If the Court upholds the ordinance the City can
immediately start to enforce its ordinance and if the Court overturns the decision, then the
Council can repeal its ordinance.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

22. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon highlighted a recent Saddleback Valley News article on doing
business in China. She thanked reporter Christopher Yee for the article and Mayor Pro Tem
Leckness for bringing this subject to the community recently and for supporting businesses. She
also congratulated Mission Viejo resident John Kurzet who won a recipe contest for his spicy
citrus ginger ribs. She again acknowledged reporter Chris Yee for the article and announced that
he is taking over Mission Viejo reporting and she welcomed him. Council Member Reardon
stated that the Colby fire made her realize that while she is prepared for an earthquake, she is not
necessarily prepared for a fire and she is thinking about inviting OCFA to present their "Ready!
Set! Go!" program in her neighborhood. Council Member Reardon told resident Stephen
Wontrobski that she would like to talk to him after the meeting about his increased HOA
assessment and she informed him that she doesn't think it has anything to do with the special fire
protection area. She also announced that she, City Clerk Karen Hamman, and Public
Information Specialist Kelly Tokarski held a mock City Council meeting last week with the 4th
graders at Carl Hankey School. The students played Council Members, staff and members of the
public and they did a wonderful job considering whether or not to build a dog park in Mission
Viejo. Council Member Reardon noted that the kids had many good ideas but didn't really
address the cost of a dog park; instead they decided that they needed three veterinarians as well
as a dog trainer on site. In the end they voted 5-0 for the dog park and it was a wonderful

City Council Minutes  9  January 20, 2014
 opportunity to talk about personal responsibilities, costs and to teach them that the City Council
Members have to take into consideration that they represent 95,000 people. Council Member
Reardon announced that she represented the City at the 2nd Annual P.J. Ramirez luncheon and
golf tournament. P.J. was 9 years old when he died unexpectedly at the end of the spring
baseball season in 2012. The two celebrations were held on his birthday and this is the way his
family is keeping his legacy alive. Council Member Reardon concluded her comments by
thanking everyone who bought toys for NEGU Joy Jars and she shared a video of young Cade
Spinello who was diagnosed with a brain tumor three years ago.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht stated that Cade Spinello is a warrior and a wonderful example of
Never Ever Give Up (NEGU.) She told the City Attorney that she is disappointed that he
became confrontational with her. She stated that her opinion is nothing personal but she cannot
support his new law firm when the co-owner is one of the attorneys who was so heavily
sanctioned by a judge. Council Member Schlicht announced that she is grateful for District
Attorney Tony Rackauckas and she stated that he did the right thing to prosecute police officers
[in the Kelly Thomas case in Fullerton.] The verdict was not what many expected and she thinks
it's now going to be up to police officers to go beyond the union and the protection of bad
cops. She also discussed the court decision on the sex offender laws for public parks. Council
Member Schlicht stated that we are becoming a nation of man instead of a nation of laws and sex
offenders’ civil rights are outweighing the rights of a child. She noted that we hear about sex
offenders being rehabbed but their victims can never get past what they did and she hopes there
is victory in the higher court. Council Member Schlicht outlined her attendance at recent events
including Let's Celebrate America! One Nation Under God! and the Saddleback Republican
Assembly roundtable event. She also encouraged people to get involved and educate themselves
on the Common Core school curriculum, she discussed her attendance at the Jenny Finch softball
camp and she wished her Mom a happy birthday tomorrow. She further announced an upcoming
Free Speech Picnic on Saturday, February 8, 2014, at C. Russell Cook Park in San Juan
Capistrano. Council Member Schlicht noted that the event will celebrate that a Judge restored
the Community Common Sense newspaper to city property in San Juan and there are 20,000
issues of the newspaper in Mission Viejo that will provide an update on that. She noted that she
will submit, for the public record, backup data to explain her reason for voting the way she did
on the cattery. She feels that giving the City of Laguna Niguel credit for a donation that was
given to the citizens of Mission Viejo was wrong. Council Member Schlicht discussed her vote
to oppose the check registers simply because she doesn't know what is happening with the
International Tennis Federation (ITF.) The Council approved the wheelchair tennis event with
the promise, by staff, that there would be sponsors and she doesn't know if that came
through. She pointed to the Mission Viejo Foundation which was supposed to generate a million
dollars yet they fell short and still owe the taxpayers $100,000. She stated that she is concerned
that if the sponsorships were not given prior to the ITF wheelchair tennis event, she doesn't know
who would pay after the fact. Council Member Schlicht congratulated Sharon Campbell and
Wayne Tate and stated that they deserve most of the credit for saving the taxpayers $42 million
in Mello Roos fees. She noted that Sharon was a bulldog on the issue and she thanked the CUSD
Board Members for seeing the light. She also thanked Tony Rackauckas for going to trial in the
Kelly Thomas case and she announced that LAPD officers will begin wearing body cameras on
City Council Minutes  10  January 20, 2014
 patrol and she'll be watching how that goes. In conclusion and in honor of Kelly Thomas,
Council Member Schlicht quoted Mark Twain: "No country can be well governed unless its
citizens as a body keep religiously before their minds that they are the guardians of the law and
that the law officers are only the machinery for its execution, nothing more."

Council Member Ury

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness announced that he likes the idea of lighting city hall in red to foster
awareness about the American Heart Association. It would have a high impact when people
drive by and he asked his colleagues for support. By consensus, the Council agreed to consider
options at the next Council Meeting. Mayor Pro Tem Leckness thanked Orange County Register
reporter Chris Yee for covering the Council Meeting and he welcomed him to the City. He also
expressed concern about fire maps and announced that a friend told him that if a homeowner is
late on their insurance payment, the insurance company could drop them. Mayor Pro Tem
Leckness stated that it is great news that sales tax revenues are skyrocketing in Mission Viejo
and property values are also going up. He thanked Director of Administrative Services Cheryl
Dyas for sending him that information. He also announced that a week ago, he was in the city of
Compton on business and it was interesting to see what life is like outside of Mission Viejo. In
Compton, the streets have gigantic potholes, there is graffiti everywhere and businesses and
homes look rundown. Mayor Pro Tem Leckness stated that it was incredible what he saw there
and he did some research and found that Compton is the least safe city in California and they
have one homicide about every four days. He sent the Mayor of Compton an email and he
would like to connect with that City to see if we can somehow help them. Mayor Pro Tem
Leckness agreed with Council Member Schlicht on the Kelly Thomas verdict and he stated that
he thinks it was terrible. He also thanked Council Member Schlicht for sharing the baseball rule
that it is a player's job to get to first base and the team's job to get the player home.

Mayor Kelley

23. 30th Anniversary of 1984 Bicycle Olympic Road Races

  Mayor Kelley presented her agenda report.

  Council Member Schlicht recommended that the Community Services Commission plan
  the event.

  Mayor Kelley stated that the Commission can certainly be included in the planning but
  since they only meet once a month, staff will be better equipped to head up the planning
  committee.

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to plan a ceremony and
  events to commemorate the 30th anniversary of the 1984 Olympic Bicycle Races.

City Council Minutes  11  January 20, 2014
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

Mayor Kelley reminded residents that Governor Brown has declared a drought in Southern
California and we need to individually and as a community, take steps to limit water use. She
noted that the City has put out a blog and eNewsletter article with simple tips to help residents
save water. Mayor Kelley stated that today is the day the nation observes the birthday of Martin
Luther King and she read her favorite quote from his dream speech: "I have a dream that my
four little children will one day live in a nation where they will not be judged by the color of
their skin, but by the content of their character." Mayor Kelley noted that it is a good reminder
for us to honor and recognize how far we have come with Dr. King's dream and she outlined her
attendance at a Martin Luther King service at Mission Viejo Christian Church. There were many
nationalities represented and fifteen church pastors and Mayor Kelley stated that it was a really
good reminder of why we recognize this day. She thanked Pastor Mike Maiolo and Mission
Viejo Christian Church for hosting the event. She also thanked and welcomed the new Orange
County Register reporter, Chris Yee. She stated that the former reporter, Mona Shadia, did a
great job of covering the City and she knows that Mr. Yee will do a great job as well. Mayor
Kelley concluded her comments with a reminder that the Community of Character word for the
month of January is perseverance and she quoted Norman Vincent Peale: "If you want to get
somewhere you have to know where you want to go and how to get there. Then never, never,
never give up."

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 10:57 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting to Monday, February 3, 2014, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of February 3, 2014

City Council Minutes  12  January 20, 2014
